# Key-Value Store

**Keep a setting without making a collection.** Your app's title, a feature switch, the prompts your page sends a
model, the last time a job ran: each is one value, not a table of records. `$kv` stores it under a name and gives it
back:

```ts
const settings = $kv.get("storytime/settings") ?? { title: "Story Time", minutes: 10 }
```

```go
var settings Settings
found, err := kvv1.Get(app, "storytime/settings", &settings)
```

There's no collection to create and no migration to write. Values live in PocketBase's own `_params` table, beside its
settings, so they ride along in every backup. It's built into `pocketone` and on by default.

The examples show each thing in TypeScript, as [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/overview) page code or `pb_hooks`, and in
Go. The Go examples use the contract's helpers (`kvv1` is `pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/kv/v1`).

## Read and write values

A value is anything JSON can hold: an object, a list, a string, a number, `true` or `false`.

```ts
$kv.set("storytime/settings", { title: "Story Time", minutes: 10, voices: ["alloy"] })

const s = $kv.get("storytime/settings") // { title: "Story Time", minutes: 10, voices: ["alloy"] }
const none = $kv.get("storytime/nothing") // null: no value under that name

$kv.delete("storytime/settings") // no error when there was nothing to delete
```

```go
err := kvv1.Set(app, "storytime/settings", Settings{Title: "Story Time", Minutes: 10})

var s Settings
found, err := kvv1.Get(app, "storytime/settings", &s) // found is false, and s untouched, when there's no value

err = kvv1.Delete(app, "storytime/settings")
```

Every call is quick and local (one read or write of your app's database), so `$kv` has no `Async` forms. `set`
replaces the whole value: to change one field, read the value, change it and set it again.

## Defaults until someone changes them

A common shape: ship defaults with your app, and store a value only once someone changes something.

```ts
const defaults = { title: "Story Time", minutes: 10 }

// read: the stored settings over the defaults
const settings = { ...defaults, ...($kv.get("storytime/settings") ?? {}) }

// save: only what the form sent
$kv.set("storytime/settings", { ...settings, minutes: Number(body.minutes) })
```

Merging over the defaults means a field you add in a later version gets its default on apps that saved settings
before it existed.

## List values

Names can share a prefix, and `list` returns every value whose name starts with it, sorted by name:

```ts
$kv.list("storytime/")
// [{ name: "storytime/settings", value: {...}, created: "2026-11-22T10:00:00Z", updated: "..." }, ...]
```

```go
entries, err := kvv1.List(app, "storytime/") // each has Name, Value (JSON), Created, Updated
```

`$kv.list()` with no prefix returns every value in the store.

## Names

A name is 1 to 128 characters: letters, digits and `_ - . : /`, starting with a letter or digit. Start yours with a
prefix of your own, such as your app's or extension's name (`storytime/settings`), so they never meet another
extension's. A name that breaks these rules throws (in Go, returns `kvv1.ErrInvalidName`).

Names starting with `_` are private to Go code on the app. Extensions keep their secrets there (LLM's provider keys
are `_llm/settings`): `$kv`, the API and agents can't read, change or list them.

A value is at most 1 MiB of JSON. For more than that, or for many similar things you want to filter, sort or let users
own, use a collection.

## From outside the app

Superusers can read and change values from the API, the `pocketone` command and agents, for example to fix a setting
on a live app:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" "https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1?prefix=storytime/"           # list
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" "https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1/get?name=storytime/settings" # one value
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -d '{"name":"storytime/settings","value":{"minutes":15}}' \
  https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1/set
curl -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -d '{"name":"storytime/settings"}' https://app.example.com/api/_c/kv/v1/delete
```

`$TOKEN` is a superuser's token, or an [API token](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens) with the `kv:read` scope (list, get) or
`kv` (all four). From your project folder, `pocketone remote kv` does the same on the project's remote:

```bash
pocketone remote kv list --prefix storytime/
pocketone remote kv get --name storytime/settings
pocketone remote kv set --name storytime/settings --value '{"minutes":15}'   # --value @settings.json reads a file
pocketone remote kv delete --name storytime/settings
```

Agents get them as MCP tools (`kv_list`, `kv_get`, `kv_set`, `kv_delete`). Users and guests can't reach the store:
your page code decides what, if anything, they see.

## Good to know

- **Where values live:** the value named `storytime/settings` is the `_params` row with id `kv:storytime/settings`.
  The `kv:` prefix keeps your names apart from PocketBase's own rows (its `settings`) and from rows other extensions
  keep there. Read and write through `$kv` or the helpers, never the table.
- **Transactions:** the Go helpers take any `core.App`, so inside `app.RunInTransaction` pass the transaction's app and
  the write is part of it. `$kv`, like `$app`, writes through the main app.
- **Turning it off:** `kv: {enabled: false}` in `pocketone.yaml` removes `$kv` and the API. The Go helpers keep
  working, since they need nothing but the database.
